headline: ACC seeks records in corruption probe involving Asif Mahmud
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has requested appointment, promotion, and transfer records from the Youth and Sports Ministry regarding allegations against the former advisor.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has written to the Ministry of Youth and Sports requesting four types of documents to investigate allegations of irregularity and corruption involving former interim government advisor Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan.

The ACC has requested the ministry to send the required documents to its head office by September 10. The probe also involves former Secretary Md. Mahbub-ul-Alam, Joint Secretary Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Zubaid Hossain, and Deputy Secretary Md. Masum Ahmed.
Allegations suggest that 7.6 million BDT was taken to cancel the current duties of 38 Upazila Youth Development Officers and appoint them to new positions.

Furthermore, it is alleged that 15 million BDT was collected from 150 Assistant Upazila Youth Development Officers for promotions, and another 20 million BDT was exchanged for postings in preferred locations.
The ACC's investigation team, led by Deputy Director Md. Zahid Kalam, was formed on Wednesday to look into these claims.

The probe is investigating whether a syndicate was formed with the support of the former advisor, involving top ministry officials and dishonest officers of the Department of Youth Development to facilitate these trades in transfers and promotions.
caption:
ACC probes corruption allegations involving former advisor Asif Mahmud and top ministry officials.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has written to the Ministry of Youth and Sports requesting four types of documents to investigate allegations of irregularity and corruption involving former interim government advisor Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan.

The ACC has requested the ministry to send the required documents to its head office by September 10. The probe also involves former Secretary Md. Mahbub-ul-Alam, Joint Secretary Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Zubaid Hossain, and Deputy Secretary Md. Masum Ahmed.

Allegations suggest that 7.6 million BDT was taken to cancel the current duties of 38 Upazila Youth Development Officers and appoint them to new positions.

Furthermore, it is alleged that 15 million BDT was collected from 150 Assistant Upazila Youth Development Officers for promotions, and another 20 million BDT was exchanged for postings in preferred locations.

The ACC's investigation team, led by Deputy Director Md. Zahid Kalam, was formed on Wednesday to look into these claims.

The probe is investigating whether a syndicate was formed with the support of the former advisor, involving top ministry officials and dishonest officers of the Department of Youth Development to facilitate these trades in transfers and promotions.

headline_marked: Wheelchair-bound Mirza Abbas [[returns to Parliament after 2 decades]]
headline: Wheelchair-bound Mirza Abbas returns to Parliament after 2 decades
summary: The BNP lawmaker and PM's Political Adviser delivered an emotional maiden speech in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad after undergoing brain surgery and treatment abroad.
details: BNP lawmaker and Prime Minister's Political Adviser Mirza Abbas returned to the parliament today, entering the chamber in a wheelchair after undergoing extensive medical treatment abroad.
In an emotional maiden speech at the 13th Jatiya Sangsad, Abbas expressed gratitude to his colleagues and sought prayers for his health so he could continue serving the people and the country.
He described the occasion as 'deeply emotional and historic,' noting that it had been nearly two decades since he last had the opportunity to speak in the chamber as a member of parliament.
Abbas also thanked the President, the Prime Minister, and the Prime Minister's Office for their support and regular check-ins during his illness.
A veteran politician, Abbas previously served as the Mayor of the undivided Dhaka City Corporation and as the Housing and Public Works Minister from 2001 to 2006.
He was elected from the Dhaka-8 constituency in the February 12 polls and took oath as an MP on February 17, shortly before falling seriously ill.
On March 11, he collapsed during iftar, which led to brain surgery in Dhaka and subsequent air ambulance transfer to Singapore and Malaysia for rehabilitation.
He was treated at Singapore General Hospital and later transferred to the Prince Court Medical Centre in Malaysia for physiotherapy and rehabilitation.
caption:
After nearly 20 years, Mirza Abbas returns to the heart of Bangladesh's democracy in a wheelchair.

BNP lawmaker and Prime Minister's Political Adviser Mirza Abbas returned to the parliament today, entering the chamber in a wheelchair after undergoing extensive medical treatment abroad.

In an emotional maiden speech at the 13th Jatiya Sangsad, Abbas expressed gratitude to his colleagues and sought prayers for his health so he could continue serving the people and the country.

He described the occasion as 'deeply emotional and historic,' noting that it had been nearly two decades since he last had the opportunity to speak in the chamber as a member of parliament.

Abbas also thanked the President, the Prime Minister, and the Prime Minister's Office for their support and regular check-ins during his illness.

A veteran politician, Abbas previously served as the Mayor of the undivided Dhaka City Corporation and as the Housing and Public Works Minister from 2001 to 2006.

He was elected from the Dhaka-8 constituency in the February 12 polls and took oath as an MP on February 17, shortly before falling seriously ill.

On March 11, he collapsed during iftar, which led to brain surgery in Dhaka and subsequent air ambulance transfer to Singapore and Malaysia for rehabilitation.

He was treated at Singapore General Hospital and later transferred to the Prince Court Medical Centre in Malaysia for physiotherapy and rehabilitation.
